correctness.rationale: In dimensionless time the dissipator is −η ad(J_z)² with η=Γ/(2NΩ). The spin-j operator representation contains one copy of each rank 0 through 2j, so rank two exists for every j≥1. Reflection in tensor index q block-diagonalizes rank two into a two-site odd chain and a three-site even chain. The determinants are p_−=z²+5ηz+4η²+1 and p_+=z³+5ηz²+(4η²+4)z+12η. Their discriminants are 9η²−4 and 16Q(η²), Q(s)=9s³−103s²+4s−16. Q is negative on [0,10] by the stated polynomial bounds and strictly increasing on [10,∞), with Q(12)>0. At its unique positive zero the depressed-cubic linear coefficient 4−13η²/3 is nonzero, so the repeated root is double. In each block the nonzero adjacent couplings determine an eigenvector from its first component, so each double eigenvalue is defective. Rank one has −η and the roots of z²+ηz+1, all real for η≥2. For η>0 any rank-two eigenvalue has Re z=−η||K_z u||²/||u||²<0: the only vector in ker K_z is the q=0 direction, which K_x does not preserve. The state I/(2j+1)+εQ_zz is physical for sufficiently small positive ε. Its Q_zz response uses the q=0 resolvent numerator N(z)=(z+η)(z+4η)+1. Since p_+=zN+3(z+4η) and N(−4η)=1, neither simple nonreal root cancels. Thus the physical signal has a damped oscillatory term throughout 2<η<η_*.
residual_risks: In the source's witness calculation the response prefactor is ε tr(Q_zz²); it is positive only when ε>0, which is an allowed choice and sufficient for the finding. Finite computations are not the all-j proof. No statement is made about ranks above two or persistent oscillations.
